{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVIgqiM8AAAABXcYQng", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm76XzhBAkq8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm76X", "number": 13, "title": "Support controlled training-data size and quality experiments for Qwen LoRA", "body": "## Problem

The current Qwen3-4B LoRA workflow prepares its training data from a pinned MBPP source and hard-coded task-ID ranges (601–974). It cannot directly import a larger, independently sourced corpus or perform a controlled comparison of training data quantity, quality, and diversity.

Previous measurements showed no reproducible coding improvement using the corrected PAD mask: with 50 steps, learning rate 1e-6, and seeds 43/44/45, the LoRA models averaged 84.07% on a 159-task HumanEval cohort versus the base model's 84.28%. Repeated tuning has already used the MBPP internal validation tasks and the HumanEval/MBPP test results. Changing only a prompt to Codex is not enough to obtain a rigorous 300/1,000/3,000-example study with the current dataset pipeline.

## Expected outcome

Extend the existing Apple Silicon / MLX-LM workflow with **reproducible, auditable experiments on the effect of Python code-generation training-data size and quality**. Prepare nested 300, 1,000, and 3,000-example training subsets where sufficient suitable data exist, alongside a same-size comparison of baseline-selected versus quality-filtered/diversity-balanced examples. Measure against a development evaluation split not previously tuned on; freeze a genuinely untouched final evaluation set before inspecting any results. Report data coverage and limitations honestly rather than assuming that more examples must improve accuracy.

Retain the same Qwen checkpoint, corrected PAD loss masking, and secure Docker-based scoring. Reuse existing project functionality rather than building a new training framework.

## Context

- Repository: `takahirox/llm-finetuning`, default branch `main`. See [README](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/README.md), [Issue #9](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/issues/9), and the existing [padding-loss experiment](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/padding-loss-experiment.md).
- Current `scripts.experiment prepare-data` assumes an immutable MBPP file, fixed MBPP task IDs, and an internal MBPP validation split. `train` and `evaluate` verify these manifests. Changes are needed for datasets beyond the small MBPP training pool.
- Related [Issue #11 / PR #12](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/pull/12) concerns HumanEval evaluation across training seeds and may still be in review. Inspect its actual merge status and reuse its evaluator/provenance features if merged. **Do not overwrite or duplicate that PR's changes**.
- Prior MBPP validation/test and HumanEval items have been repeatedly inspected. They are historical diagnostics, **not untouched final confirmation sets** for choosing the new training data.
- Follow the repository's [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/llm-finetuning/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md). Use English for new Issue/PR/docs.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Pinned, quality-audited data ingestion
- [ ] Research and select one or more legitimate, accessible Python task/solution datasets suitable for at least 3,000 unique training examples. Document their canonical source URL, immutable version/revision/checksums, license, attribution, format, and any redistribution/usage restrictions. Verify actual usable counts **before** claiming 3,000 examples are available. If a compliant source cannot supply the target number, document the constraint and avoid fabricating or silently duplicating examples.
- [ ] Implement a minimal external-dataset preparation path yielding the existing MLX-LM conversation/JSONL format, plus deterministic split manifests and sample-level provenance. Preserve the original MBPP workflow. Store downloaded corpora and generated splits only in ignored local paths.
- [ ] Reject missing/invalid solutions, duplicate or near-duplicate problem/solution pairs (within and across sources), and obvious non-Python or low-quality entries using reproducible, documented rules. Preserve filter reasons/counts and dataset quality/diversity diagnostics (e.g. task categories, length, dependencies, testability). Do not silently execute arbitrary external solutions on the host; if running tests, use the existing bounded isolated Docker approach.
- [ ] Check overlap against the project's past MBPP/HumanEval training and evaluation examples and any proposed new evaluation sets, including normalized text/code similarity where feasible; record exclusions and remaining uncertain semantic overlap. Public pretraining contamination cannot be ruled out.

### Controlled size-versus-quality comparison
- [ ] Generate **nested** training sets of 300, 1,000, and 3,000 distinct examples from the same eligible corpus (the smaller set must be included in the next larger one), with fixed selection seed, immutable sample IDs and hashes, and a manifest verifying counts and relationships. Keep validation/evaluation items separate.
- [ ] Provide at least one **same-size** 300-example quality/diversity comparison (e.g. deterministic unfiltered eligible sample versus quality-filtered/diversity-balanced sample) from the same source pool. Explicitly document the filter or selection criterion; do not claim that changing the corpus and quantity simultaneously isolates quality.
- [ ] Use the corrected padding mask, same base model/revision, LoRA rank/layers, optimizer family and fixed decoding/scorer settings. Start from the previous reasonable learning rate `1e-6` unless a documented preregistered change is essential. Seed and training policy must be explicit.
- [ ] Address **training exposure and compute fairness**: a 50-step, batch-1 run samples far fewer than 3,000 examples and is not by itself a valid 3,000-example exposure experiment. Record dataset order, actual samples/tokens seen, truncation and reuse; choose and explain comparable fixed-compute and/or fixed-epoch protocols, including any unavoidable compute differences. Do not describe size effects if the stated dataset was never actually sampled as designed.
- [ ] Keep each run's adapters, config, source fingerprints, logs and results in separate ignored paths; do not overwrite or mutate any existing model weights, historical datasets, adapters or reports.

### Evaluation, reporting and safeguards
- [ ] Establish a development scoring set that does not overlap with any train subset and was not used for the previous hyperparameter selection, and define a **separately locked, untouched** confirmation set before viewing experiment outcomes. Use an appropriate benchmark/task format compatible with the existing sandbox, with pinned source/licenses. Never use the earlier MBPP 500 or HumanEval results as a new training-set selection target.
- [ ] Evaluate the adapter-free base model and all applicable experimental adapters with identical held-out questions, generation parameters, Docker execution and scoring. Include pass@1, passed/total, delta versus base, paired fail→pass/pass→fail changes, errors/format failures, and uncertainty/seed variability if replicated. Record corpus characteristics and effective training exposure for every run.
- [ ] Report size effects and quality effects **separately**, acknowledge differences in compute exposure, public-benchmark contamination and multiple comparisons, and avoid claims of general improvement from one internal split. Freeze any choice made using development results and only then perform a one-time independent confirmation.
- [ ] Add focused tests for source/checksum validation, selection/deduplication and nested subset invariants, split/leakage checks, manifest integrity, run provenance, fair-exposure accounting, and compatible evaluation/comparison. Run applicable tests, syntax and dependency checks before merge; report any real-device runs not performed.
- [ ] Add concise English README/docs instructions for sourcing, preparing, training, evaluation and comparison, including a reasonable small smoke test. Keep implementation narrowly scoped, use an Issue-linked PR to `main`, and comply with the existing review/merge guidance.

## Optional validation

- If a capable Apple Silicon machine, the external datasets and evaluation harness are accessible, execute the real 300/1,000/3,000 size study and same-size quality study. Record real wall time, memory pressure, dataset coverage, pass@1, and per-task changes; do not invent measurements if the implementation environment cannot run the experiments.
- Replicate the most informative development comparisons across multiple independent training seeds before the frozen independent final evaluation. Avoid excessive sweeps or retroactive tuning to the final set.

## Required post-merge verification

None automatically required. Merging does not initiate training or publication. Document any unperformed full experiment as a future local execution rather than a passed merge check.
